article_text:
Gang Dong-won and Kim Go-eun will lead The Twilight Between Us , an action-romance period drama for Netflix.

Kim Won-suk ( When Life Gives You Tangerines ) is directing a script from writer Park Ji-eun ( Queen on Tears ) about heirs to a pair of houses locked in a century-long feud who are forced into marriage by royal decree. Further production and casting details haven’t been released at this stage.

The story follows Mu-yeong (Gang) and Su-ryeon (Kim), whose union is intended to end generations on conflict. However, it soon spirals in unforeseen directions.

Related Stories

'VisionQuest' Teases Surprise 'Avengers: Doomsday' Character Return In Post-Credits Scene

'Dancing With The Stars' Recap: Dance Offs On Grammy Night Bring Tough Competition To Quarterfinals

Mu-yeong, the illegitimate son of the House of Kang, carries the ominous title ‘Demon of the North’ and live sin obscurity despite his exceptional martial skill and noble heart. Su-ryeon, the only daughter of House Han, finds herself bound by a royal marriage ban after failing to become the Crown Princess, until her union with Mu-yeong changes her fate.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix is also today announcing reality competition series Vocal Class Wars has gone into production ahead of a 2027 launch date.

The series follows on from Netflix’s existing Culinary Class Wars and is billed as a “vocal survival competition that pits ‘White Singers’ – who the producers are calling ‘established artists whose names alone define a genre’ – against ‘Black Singers’ – challengers who erase their names and identities to prove their worth through voice alone. A similar black-and-white format device was used in Culinary Class Wars .

The series reunites Kim Hak-min, the producer behind Culinary Class Wars , and Park Sung-hwan, the producer who devised the Just Makeup beauty-survival format, following their previous collaboration on Sing Again . Studio Slam is making the show, with Choi Hye-jung attached to write.

The Vocal Class Wars production team said: “Following Culinary Class Wars , we’re excited to expand the ‘black-and-white’ universe to a new stage — music. Watch for whether the legendary artists appearing as ‘White Singers’ can protect their reputation, or whether the ‘Black Singers’ set to shock the world will flip the script — expect another thrilling showdown and unpredictable twists in this next class war.”

editorial_title_zh: 正义记忆化为艺术：玛丽亚·多梅尼卡·拉皮卡沃利讲述“大审判”的故事
editorial_excerpt_zh: 卷宗、笔录与文件成为摄影装置的主角，重新将反黑组的司法工作置于中心。展览在卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆展出至26日 文章标题：正义记忆化为艺术：玛丽亚…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "一场审判在集体记忆中留下了什么？档案又如何能还原这起标志着意大利历史的司法案件的分量？在巴勒莫“大审判”启动四十年之际，玛丽亚·多梅尼卡·拉皮卡沃利（Maria Domenica Rapicavoli）的项目通过那些曾协助重建黑手党结构档案的影像，再次提出了这些问题。2026年10月4日至11月26日，巴勒莫省的卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆（Museo Civico di Castelbuono）将举办由劳拉·巴雷卡（Laura Barreca）和乔瓦娜·菲乌梅（Giovanna Fiume）策展的艺术家摄影装置展《MAXIPROCESSO》，并由Supervoid建筑事务所负责布展，同时放映由帕斯夸莱·西梅卡（Pasquale Scimeca）执导的纪录片《大审判》（1986–2026）。", "links": [{"text": "Palermo", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/palermo/"}, {"text": "Maria Domenica Rapicavoli", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/maria-domenica-rapicavoli/"}, {"text": "Museo Civico di Castelbuono", "url": "https://www.museocivico.eu/"}, {"text": "Supervoid", "url": "https://www.supervoid.eu/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该项目由卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆构思，延续了2026年6月在巴勒莫法院与司法机构合作下开幕的展览路线。展览的核心是三十幅将“大审判”的卷宗和司法文件推向前景的摄影作品，将档案材料转化为具有强烈视觉冲击力的实体呈现，并将这些影像还原为具有非凡比例的调查和诉讼工作的具体维度：在由乔瓦尼·法尔科内（Giovanni Falcone）协调的反黑组指示下收集的数千条数据、司法合作者的审讯笔录、监听记录以及与黑手党活动相关的文件。该项目于2026年9月21日荣获第三十一届罗萨里奥·利瓦蒂诺-安东尼诺·萨埃塔-加埃塔诺·科斯塔纪念国际社会承诺奖（XXXI Premio Internazionale all’Impegno Sociale, Memorial Rosario Livatino-Antonino Saetta-Gaetano Costa）。该奖项因该倡议的公民与社会价值颁发给劳拉·巴雷卡、乔瓦娜·菲乌梅和玛丽亚·D·拉皮卡沃利。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/MAXIPROCESSO_Martina-Rapicavoli_3-1024x686.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "玛丽亚·D·拉皮卡沃利（Maria D. Rapicavoli），《MAXIPROCESSO》，2015-2018年，三十幅摄影冲印件，Supervoid装置，2026年，卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆藏品。该项目获得由文化部当代创意总局推广的“摄影战略2025”公开招标资助。", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在1976年出生于卡塔尼亚、现活跃于纽约的拉皮卡沃利的创作中，摄影成为了质问权力结构及其对个人和集体生活影响的工具。通过一种交织摄影、录像、雕塑和装置的语言，艺术家深入调查了政治、经济和犯罪系统，常常聚焦于那些保持隐形或处于公众叙事边缘的事物。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由安娜·利维亚·弗里埃尔（Anna Livia Friel）、本杰明·加列戈斯·加比隆多（Benjamin Gallegos Gabilondo）和马尔科·普罗温切亚利（Marco Provinciali）领导的罗马事务所Supervoid操刀的布展设计，呼应了关于建筑、权力和机构之间关系的思考。该项目也融入了该事务所正在进行的关于巴勒莫地堡法庭（Aula Bunker）的研究之中，后者是举行“大审判”的标志性地点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/MAXIPROCESSO_Martina-D.-Rapicavoli_2-1024x681.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "玛丽亚·D·拉皮卡沃利（Maria D. Rapicavoli），《MAXIPROCESSO》，2015-2018年，三十幅摄影冲印件，Supervoid装置，2026年，卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆藏品。该项目获得由文化部当代创意总局推广的“摄影战略2025”公开招标资助。", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拓展展览路线的是帕斯夸莱·西梅卡执导的纪录片《大审判》（1986–2026），该片为纪念该审判于1986年2月10日启动四十周年而作。通过档案影像，该片重构了该诉讼程序中最具意义的一些时刻，这些时刻从司法上确认了黑手党是一个有组织的系统。摄影与纪录片由此在历史文献与对这一在某种程度上继续质问当下公民良知的事件的当代阐释之间构建起一场对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览伴随着由玛丽亚·罗莎·索萨伊（Maria Rosa Sossai）策划的一系列公共倡议和参与性活动，包括学校的参与、对事件主角的采访，以及与DIECIMEDIA机构合作通过社交网络进行的传播行动，以将“大审判”的知识推广到更年轻的世代，使记忆成为一种对抗和觉醒的工具。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为卡斯特尔布ونو市立博物馆当代艺术永久收藏的一部分，该装置注定将继续其巡展行程，后续阶段预计将在罗马、特拉帕尼和米兰举行。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Che cosa resta di un processo nella memoria collettiva? E in che modo gli archivi possono restituire la portata di una vicenda giudiziaria che ha segnato la storia italiana? A quarant’anni dall’avvio del Maxiprocesso di Palermo , il progetto di Maria Domenica Rapicavoli torna a interrogare con queste domande attraverso le immagini degli atti che contribuirono a ricostruire la struttura di Cosa Nostra. Dal 4 ottobre al 26 novembre 2026, il Museo Civico di Castelbuono , in provincia di Palermo, ospita MAXIPROCESSO , l’installazione fotografica dell’artista a cura di Laura Barreca e Giovanna Fiume , con un allestimento dello studio di architettura Supervoid e la proiezione del documentario Il Maxiprocesso (1986–2026) , diretto da Pasquale Scimeca .

Il progetto, ideato dal Museo Civico di Castelbuono, prosegue il percorso espositivo inaugurato nel giugno 2026 al Palazzo di Giustizia di Palermo, in collaborazione con le istituzioni giudiziarie. Al centro della mostra sono trenta fotografie che portano in primo piano faldoni e documenti giudiziari del Maxiprocesso, trasformando materiali d’archivio in presenze visive di forte impatto e restituendo alle immagini la dimensione concreta di un lavoro investigativo e processuale di proporzioni straordinarie: migliaia di dati, verbali degli interrogatori dei collaboratori di giustizia, intercettazioni e documenti relativi alle attività mafiose, raccolti nell’ambito dell’istruttoria condotta dal pool antimafia coordinato da Giovanni Falcone . Il progetto ha ricevuto il 21 settembre 2026 il XXXI Premio Internazionale all’Impegno Sociale, Memorial Rosario Livatino-Antonino Saetta-Gaetano Costa. Il riconoscimento è stato assegnato a Laura Barreca, Giovanna Fiume e Maria D. Rapicavoli per il valore civile e sociale dell’iniziativa.

Nella ricerca di Rapicavoli, nata a Catania nel 1976 e oggi attiva a New York, la fotografia diventa uno strumento per interrogare le strutture del potere e le loro conseguenze sulla vita individuale e collettiva. Attraverso un linguaggio che attraversa fotografia, video, scultura e installazione, l’artista indaga sistemi politici, economici e criminali, concentrandosi spesso su ciò che rimane invisibile o ai margini della narrazione pubblica.

L’allestimento firmato da Supervoid, studio romano diretto da Anna Livia Friel , Benjamin Gallegos Gabilondo e Marco Provinciali , accompagna questa riflessione sul rapporto tra architettura, potere e istituzioni. Il progetto si inserisce inoltre in una ricerca che lo studio sta dedicando all’Aula Bunker di Palermo, luogo emblematico della celebrazione del Maxiprocesso.

Ad ampliare il percorso è il documentario Il Maxiprocesso (1986–2026) di Pasquale Scimeca, realizzato in occasione del quarantesimo anniversario dell’avvio del processo, il 10 febbraio 1986. Attraverso immagini d’archivio, il film ricostruisce alcuni dei momenti più significativi di un procedimento che riconobbe giudiziariamente la mafia come un sistema organizzato. Fotografie e documentario costruiscono così un dialogo tra documentazione storica e interpretazione contemporanea di una vicenda che continua in qualche modo a interrogare la coscienza civile del presente.

La mostra si accompagna a un programma di iniziative pubbliche e attività partecipative curate da Maria Rosa Sossai , con il coinvolgimento delle scuole, interviste ai protagonisti delle vicende e azioni di divulgazione anche attraverso i social network, in collaborazione con l’agenzia DIECIMEDIA, per estendere la conoscenza del Maxiprocesso alle generazioni più giovani, facendo della memoria uno strumento di confronto e consapevolezza.

Entrata nella collezione permanente di arte contemporanea del Museo Civico di Castelbuono, l’installazione è destinata a proseguire il suo itinerario, con successive tappe previste a Roma, Trapani e Milano.

article_text:
Issue

Whispering Gallery: The Collectors Are Coming. Possibly.

CC WANG

Still no word on who will take the wheel at Phillips Asia in Hong Kong after Jonathan Crockett’s departure in late August. The art market is so soft that nobody appears eager to volunteer for the charmingly impossible task of producing miracles on demand. Generally regarded as the bronze medalist in the scene, the auction house has been shedding rainmakers beyond Crockett, such as Miety Heiden in New York. The suspicion, naturally, is that the Russian-owned Mercury group is trimming the sails, cutting costs, and perhaps casting about for a new owner.

Mercury might take a leaf from Sotheby’s glossy handbook. The house has never been shy of hiring photogenic, glamorous figures, among them CC Wang , who presides over Sotheby’s Maison, described by less charitable observers as a luxury department store with an auctioneer’s stationary. But one of its more astute appointments, made during the company’s publicly traded heyday, was the quietly formidable Jen Hua . Recruited in 2013 by Kevin Ching, then chief executive of Sotheby’s Asia, and Patti Wong, its former chairwoman, Hua has since established herself as a power broker of the old-fashioned sort, keeping Sotheby’s performing in Greater China even as reports suggest Chinese collectors have been keeping their wallets closer to their chests. Now deputy chairwoman of Sotheby’s Asia and chairwoman of China, she is also the house’s discreet political ace, being the granddaughter of the former Chinese leader Hua Guofeng.

article_text:
Jusqu’au 5 décembre 2026, LaCinetek met à disposition, dans son abonnement, deux films documentaires de Raymond Depardon : Faits divers (1983) et Délits flagrants (1994). Une plongée dans la police, puis dans la justice parisienne, et un cinéaste qui laisse tourner la caméra au plus près du réel.

Raymond Depardon, ce « photographe-cinéaste », toujours renversant de précision, à l’affût du réel, au contact des gens et de ce qui se passe, est, à l’occasion du mois du documentaire de la plateforme LaCinetek, mis en lumière à travers deux de ses films : Faits divers (1983) et Délits flagrants (1994). Deux œuvres en diptyque, se répondant et se complétant malgré plus de dix ans d’écart.

Dans le premier, nous plongeons dans le quotidien d’une brigade de police du 5e arrondissement de Paris. Du commissariat aux rues, en passant par les espaces intimes, les plans durent et glacent parfois le sang. Nous assistons à la déposition d’une femme qui vient porter plainte pour viol et que l’on réprimande sur un ton paternaliste, puis nous restons figés dans un appartement, où une autre femme, allongée sur un lit, inanimée, est victime d’une overdose . Les silences, les regards, le souffle du policier qui s’accélère à la vue de ce corps à la lisière de la mort, les plans rapprochés sur une main gorgée de sang… Raymond Depardon reste, il ne se dérobe pas, et le spectateur non plus, contraint lui aussi de regarder. C’est le cadre, et un rythme posé, qui nous enjoignent de recevoir l’image. En laissant tourner la caméra, il recueille ce qui se passe devant lui : personne ne joue, c’est criant de vérité, et tout a pourtant l’air si bien composé, comme dans ses photographies, des postures aux lumières, des couleurs aux visages marqués.

Le « parler frais »

Puis vient Délits flagrants , tourné en huis clos dans les bureaux de la 8e section du palais de justice de Paris, section disparue en 1999 avec une réorganisation du parquet. Quatorze plans-séquences montrent les confrontations entre les prévenus et les magistrat·es (les substituts du procureur), notamment Michèle Bernard-Requin, chargé·es de gérer la permanence criminelle quotidienne, de diriger les enquêtes de police urgentes et de décider immédiatement des suites judiciaires. On regarde avec précision les différents cas de figure, comme celui d’une femme jugée pour vol à l’étalage aux Galeries Lafayette, qui se fourvoie dans ses mensonges. On ressent la fatigue des journées passées dans ces bureaux clos, et des échanges teintés de malaise ou de sourires nerveux.

Ce qui ressort de ces films, c’est le dévoilement du « parler frais » , une obsession que Raymond Depardon avouait au micro de France Culture en 2017 . Le vrai, dans le langage comme à l’image, nous apparaît plus vrai que jamais, avec ses maladresses et ses bizarreries. Il est difficile d’imaginer que cette institution accepte aujourd’hui de se laisser filmer ainsi, avec autant de vérité, et l’on garde l’impression que rien n’a été coupé au montage.

Ce que ce diptyque nous dévoile aussi, c’est une fresque particulière de la France des années 1980-1990, qui prend parfois à la gorge : la misogynie, le racisme latent. Et à l’heure où d’autres images de la police nous parviennent, il y a quelque chose de déroutant à regarder celles d’hier. Raymond Depardon, pourtant, ne dénonce pas, il regarde et capte longtemps, pour nous laisser le temps, à nous aussi, de comprendre ce qui se joue de l’intérieur, et comment, peut-être, arriver à le défaire.

Faits divers et Délits flagrants sont disponibles dans l’abonnement à LaCinetek, jusqu’au 5 décembre 2026. Ce diptyque est labellisé Bicentenaire de la Photographie par le ministère de la Culture.

article_text:
More than 46 years after his big-screen debut in the slasher classic “Friday the 13th,” hulking horror icon Jason Voorhees is about to prove that his machete cuts just as deep in animation. The hockey-masked killer returns in “ Never Hike Alone : Ghosts in the Fog,” a new 10-minute animated film from independent production company Womp Stomp Films.

Premiering Friday, Nov. 13, at 5 p.m. PT, and streaming for free on the Womp Stomp Films YouTube channel, the story follows an unlucky trio of friends whose relaxing weekend camping trip takes a gory turn when they become lost in the fog surrounding the infamous Camp Crystal Lake.

Isabelle Huppert Vampire Film ‘The Blood Countess’ Was Cut Against Director’s Wishes, Ulrike Ottinger Tells Tokyo Event

Founded in 2016 by filmmaker Vincente DiSanti, Womp Stomp Films has built a devoted following with its ambitious series of “Friday the 13th” fan films. The saga began with DiSanti’s 2017 short “Never Hike Alone,” followed by the winter-set prequel “Never Hike in the Snow” in 2020. The feature-length sequel “Never Hike Alone 2” arrived in 2023, featuring “Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives” actors Thom Mathews and Vincent Guastaferro reprising their original roles as Tommy Jarvis and Sheriff Rick Cologne.

The “Never Hike Alone” films have relied on crowdfunding campaigns to help finance their increasingly elaborate productions. The fan-supported approach has allowed DiSanti and his collaborators to expand the saga while making the finished films available to watch for free online.

Although the “Never Hike Alone” films feature copyrighted characters, settings and storylines from the official “Friday the 13th” franchise, Womp Stomp Films operates independently of the studios that own the Jason Voorhees property. The company follows a set of self-imposed guidelines designed to avoid copyright disputes, including making its films available for free, using crowdfunding exclusively for production expenses and not turning a profit. Each film includes an on-screen disclaimer acknowledging that the rights holders can challenge the production. So far, the franchise owners have not taken action to stop the films.

“Ghosts in the Fog” marks the fourth installment in the Womp Stomp series and its first venture into animation. The short arrives amid a resurgence of activity surrounding the “Friday the 13th” franchise. Peacock debuted its A24-produced prequel series “Crystal Lake,” starring Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees, in October. Meanwhile, it was announced Friday that Steve Miner, who directed 1981’s “Friday the 13th Part 2” and 1982’s “Friday the 13th Part III,” will return to helm the franchise’s 13th feature film, scheduled for theatrical release in 2027. The new movie will mark Jason’s first big-screen appearance since the 2009 reboot.

“Ghosts in the Fog” was produced in collaboration with Mako Animation Studio, a Mexico-based company specializing in 2D animation. Founded in 2015 by Juan Rivera, who co-directed the new short alongside DiSanti, the studio’s previous projects include the animated YouTube series “John Death.”

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Woody Harrelson is backing his first short film.

The multi-hyphenate has boarded Mary the Widow , writer-director Ryan Noufer’s live-action short, as an executive producer. It’s the first time he’s EP’d a short, joined by Jack Piatt ( The Singers ) and Kevin McCormick.

“ Mary the Widow is a special kind of film. It doesn’t waste a second in taking hold of your heart. It captures the joy of finding your soulmate in life while never shying away from some hard truths about aging and loss. It left me with tears in my eyes. Ryan is a filmmaker to watch,” Harrelson said in a statement to Deadline on Friday.

Woody Harrelson To Play Wealthy American Expat In Freefall In Rick Alverson's 'Summer Of Roses'

Watch the full short above.

Watch on Deadline

In Mary the Widow , Julie Ariola stars as Mary, a widow who has barely left the house since her husband died. Her daughter Penny (Jean Villepique) signs her up for a speed-dating night for widows and widowers anyway. Across the table comes a man who only talks about himself, a man who will not stop talking at all, and a would-be sugar daddy. Then Ed ( Stephen Tobolowsky ) sits down. He is gentle, he is funny, and he listens. On the drive home, Mary cannot stop thinking about him, and the film quietly reveals why. Arianna Ortiz and Robert Lee Barry round out the cast.

Noufer wrote the 14-minute film for his late grandmother Mary, whose dementia shaped the story.

“This short is an ode to my late grandmother, Mary. Due to Alzheimer’s, she never quite understood I was her grandson,” Noufer said in a statement of his own. “As a child, that confused me. As an adult, it haunts me. But not all ghosts have to be bad. I hope this film is a good one.”

Switchboard will distribute the film and is campaigning it for the 99th Academy Awards as part of its 2026-27 shorts slate.

Adds Celia Aniskovich, founder of Switchboard Magazine and a producer on the film: “Ryan somehow manages to fit a whole life story into 14 minutes and takes audiences on a journey they don’t see coming. It is funny, touching, devastating, and most importantly, human. We are incredibly proud to be part of the team behind this award-winning, truly special film, and we can’t wait to share it with audiences this season.”

Mary the Widow is written and directed by Ryan Noufer and produced by Celia Aniskovich, Amina Fishburn, Brian Buxton and Trevor Alper. Executive producers are Woody Harrelson, Jack Piatt, Kevin McCormick and Sarge Anderson.

Switchboard has acquired and distributed numerous short films and documentaries including A Pocket Guide To Pigeon Watching , This Is Private , Community Theater , Mary The Widow , Oh Whale , Freeman Vines , Poreless , Rat Rod , and Saving Superman .

article_text:
Anthropic’s proposal ( AI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’, 19 October ) raises an important question: who should benefit from technological progress? Before pledging money for the public good, AI companies such as Anthropic should first pay the creators whose work they use.

Device manufacturers have a separate responsibility under the same principle: creators should share in the value their work generates. Smartphones , computers and other devices enable creative work to be copied and stored, yet UK creators receive no private-copying payments, unlike their counterparts in more than 40 other countries.

The proposed Smart Fund would require manufacturers and importers to make modest contributions on devices used to copy or store creative work. It could raise up to £300m a year, providing creators with additional income and supporting skills, cultural programmes and affordable workspaces.

For creators on persistently low and falling incomes, these payments would make a tangible difference. Visual artists’ median annual earnings are just £12,500 – 47% lower in real terms than in 2010. Authors earn a median of only £7,000 from writing, down from £11,300, according to surveys published in 2022 and 2018 respectively. Audiovisual performers report median annual earnings from performing of £17,500 . Yet it is creators’ work that attracts people to technology, sustains their engagement and drives innovation. Those creators should share in the value their work helps generate, so they can continue creating and powering that cycle. The government should turn this principle into action by introducing the Smart Fund. Barbara Hayes Chief executive, Authors’ Licensing and Collecting Society (ALCS) Tayyiba Nasser Chief executive, British Equity Collecting Society (BECS) Christian Zimmermann Chief executive, Design and Artists Copyright Society (DACS) Paul Seheult Chief executive, PICSEL

article_text:
Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya y Jason Momoa regresan en la nueva película de Denis Villeneuve, que llegará a los cines el 18 de diciembre.

El universo de Dune está de regreso. Warner Bros . presentó el tráiler final de Dune 3 , la esperada película de Denis Villeneuve que continuará la historia de Paul Atreides, interpretado por Timothée Chalamet . Con escenas cargadas de acción, conspiraciones y el regreso de los imponentes gusanos de arena, la tercera entrega promete profundizar en las consecuencias del poder y llevar la épica saga de ciencia ficción hacia un desenlace oscuro.

La película estará inspirada en El mesías de Dune, la novela de Frank Herbert , y transcurrirá 17 años después de los acontecimientos de Dune: Parte Dos . Convertido en el emperador Muad’Dib, Paul deberá afrontar las consecuencias de su ascenso al poder mientras las tensiones políticas, las traiciones y las campañas militares amenazan con desatar un nuevo conflicto. Sus visiones del futuro también se volverán cada vez más inquietantes, mientras intenta comprender el destino que le espera a él y a las personas que ama.

El avance

El tráiler anticipa una historia marcada por las conspiraciones y el costo de gobernar un imperio. En medio de la rebelión y la amenaza de sus enemigos, Chani, el personaje de Zendaya, ocupará un lugar central en los conflictos que rodean a Paul. La película explorará así el costado más sombrío del protagonista y el círculo de violencia que parece incapaz de detener.

El elenco reunirá nuevamente a Chalamet , Zendaya , Javier Bardem como Stilgar, Rebecca Ferguson como Lady Jessica y Florence Pugh como la emperatriz Irulan. También regresará Jason Momoa , esta vez como Hayt, mientras que entre las incorporaciones se encuentran Robert Pattinson como Scytale, Anya Taylor-Joy como Alia Atreides e Isaach De Bankolé como Farok.

Dune 3 llegará a los cines el 18 de diciembre y marcará una nueva etapa en la adaptación cinematográfica de la obra de Frank Herbert. Aunque Villeneuve considera que esta será su última película de la saga, el universo de Dune todavía tiene historias por explorar. Por ahora, el cineasta se prepara para cerrar su trilogía con una historia que promete combinar espectáculo visual, intrigas políticas y las consecuencias de las decisiones de Paul Atreides.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Vantage Media has acquired North American rights to Polish feature Exotic , about a woman’s journey toward self-discovery through pole dancing, ahead of its premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival .

The picture follows a writer whose quest to master pole dancing evolves into something far more profound when the process and community of dancers she encounters help her figure out her true self. It is the first feature of Sonja Orlewicz-Zakrzewska and grew out of her personal fascination with pole dancing.

The deal was negotiated by Jessica Russo, COO of Productions and Acquisitions at VMI Worldwide and Vantage Media, and Daniel Vadocky, Head of Sales at Berlin-based Pluto Film, which has also unveiled a first international trailer to coincide with the announcement. Gutek is handling the Polish release.

Related Stories

Raven Banner Boards Polish Folklore Horror 'Òpi' Ahead Of U.S. Festival Debut

Poland Selects Paweł Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland' To Compete In International Film Oscar Race

“At a time when women’s rights and freedoms are increasingly being challenged in America, Exotic delivers a timely and empowering message about the importance of embracing who we truly are,” said Russo at Vantage/VMI.

Watch on Deadline

“Through the art of dance, the film celebrates female strength, confidence and self-expression, reminding us that empowerment often begins with the courage to step outside our comfort zones. Exotic is more than a story about pole dancing; it’s a celebration of sisterhood, self-discovery, and the freedom to unapologetically be yourself.”

“We are very pleased to have secured a North American distribution deal ahead of the film’s world premiere,” added Vadocky at Pluto Film. “It is a strong sign to its international appeal and audience potential. We have full confidence that Vantage/VMI will successfully distribute the film across all platforms.”

Exotic was shot during a recent real-life edition of a pole-dancing Exo Stars Camp featuring real participants and instructors, maintaining the authenticity of this vivid bubble.

“As soon as I discovered exotic pole dance, I got so invested that I went straight to Exo Stars Camp,” explains the writer-director. “I was fascinated by the clash of the fragile, intimate universes we carried within us around the camp. It soon became clear that the camp itself was a perfect place to confront fears, leave one’s comfort zone and express oneself more than daily life ever allows. “

The film stars Jaśmina Polak, Magdalena Koleśnik and Monika Frajczyk. Director of Photography is Adam Suzin, with Tomasz Kajetan Naruszewicz as Editor and Tymek Papior as Composer.to here. It received support from the Polish Film Institute’s microbudget scheme aimed at first-time directors.

Director, scriptwriter, visual artist and photographer Orlewicz-Zakrzewska holds a master’s degree in photography from the Cinematography Department of the Łódź Film School.

Her first short, Cross’n’Carry (2019), screened at festivals including New Horizons, HollyShorts and BEAST Portugal. She also took part in the script training lab Atelier Scenariuszowe and the EAVE Producers Workshop (2021).

As a cinematographer, she worked on Enthusiasts , a documentary series for Canal+. Her video art and photography have been shown in numerous exhibitions including the Leica Gallery Warsaw.

Exotic will debut in the First Feature Competition of Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival running from November 6 to 22.

Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，在丰塔内西访日150年之际，这也是老师与弟子们的作品欢聚一堂的宝贵契机。本展除了来自意大利的作品群之外，日本国内美术馆及博物馆收藏的丰塔内西作品，以及浅井忠、小山正太郎等弟子们的作品也将汇聚一堂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/3-21.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "丰塔内西送别纪念合影 1878年拍摄 松戸市教育委員会所蔵", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "并且，本展还将对丰塔内西的前瞻性进行探讨。展厅中还将一并展出塞甘蒂尼、卡尔洛·卡拉等后世画家的作品，探讨他对20世纪意大利艺术家产生了怎样的影响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "展览结构", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第一章：“绘画”之风景（1850-1860年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在故乡雷焦艾米利亚接受专业美术教育的丰塔内西，在参加第一次意大利独立战争后，将据点转移至瑞士卢加诺，随后移至日内瓦。从对美学构图和“如画（Picturesque）”景致的追求开始，风景画家丰塔内西的历程由此起步。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/4-22.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《岩间植物》1850年前后 油彩／硬纸板 比耶拉地区博物馆（比耶拉）Archivio Fotografico ‒ Museo del Territorio Biellese", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/5-21.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《布热高原》1859‒1860年 油彩／画布 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第二章：映照心灵的风景（1855-1875年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1855年，丰塔内西与巴比松派画家特罗扬一同参观了巴黎世博会，借此机会接触到了柯罗及其他巴比松派画家的作品。以此为契机之一，丰塔内西开始创作不仅忠于自然，还融入了细腻抒情情绪的绘画。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/6-19.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《水磨坊》 1858‒1859年 油彩／画布 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/7-20.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《寂静》1860年前后 油彩／画布 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第三章：城市风景（1854-1880年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在移居瑞士、滞留英国以及游历意大利各地的过程中，丰塔内西将目光投向了城市风景。以取材自日内瓦市内的石版画为开端，丰塔内西的城市风景画在画册《伦敦素描集》中变得更加洗练。随着他旅居佛罗伦萨（期间孕育了与意大利外光派及马基雅伊奥利画派画家的交往），以及应阿尔贝蒂娜美术学院之邀移居都灵，他对城市的关注得到了进一步加强。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/8-18.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《圣玛丽亚诺韦拉大教堂》1867年前后 油彩／木板 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第四章：日常生活与自然（1860-1875年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过参加巴黎沙龙并接触罗莎·博纳尔、让-弗朗索瓦·米勒等人的绘画，丰塔内西自1860年前后起，逐渐开始探索扎根于日常生活与社会的主题。丰塔内西的作品重视农民、家畜以及人与自然的关系，这标志着他艺术生涯中的一个重要转折点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/12-15.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《劳动》1868‒1872年 油彩／画布 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第五章：描绘转瞬即逝的光（1867-1880年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丰塔内西将光影的变化与内心的起伏联系在一起。撷取乌云遮日的那一刻、将彩虹般的光芒洒向平原的瞬间的《四月》，描绘风景随着日落时光线变化而不断蜕变的沼泽风景连作――丰塔内西着眼于气象与光影的流转及其效果，对这种动荡且神秘的自然进行了细致入微的绘画创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/15-7.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《四月》1873年 油彩／画布 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/16-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《沉入沼泽的太阳》1874年前后 油彩／木板 都灵市立近现代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/17-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《沼泽落日》1876‒1878年前后 油彩／画布 三重县立美术馆", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第六章：在日本的创作与教育（1876-1878年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "被明治政府设立的工部美术学校任命为画学教师的丰塔内西于1876年8月前后抵达东京。大约两年后的1878年秋天，因健康原因及学校改革受挫等原因，丰塔内西回国。但他系统的教育尝试与热忱指导，促成了他与包括女学生在内的弟子们之间硕果累累的对话与信任关系。浅井忠、小山正太郎、松冈寿等学生将老师的教诲以各种形式进行升华，奠定了此后日本近代西洋画的基础。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/18-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《日本寺庙入口》1878‒1880年 明暗对照法／画布 雷焦艾米利亚市立博物馆 Musei Civici Reggio Emilia", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/19-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "浅井忠 《德川家灵庙Ⅰ（寺庙入口Ⅰ）》1878年左右 油彩／纸 都灵市立现代和当代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "小山正太郎《秋景图》1887年 油彩／画布 寄托于京都国立近代美术馆", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第7章：晚年作品（1878-1881年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "回国后，丰塔内西恢复了在阿尔贝蒂娜美术学院的工作。然而，在1880年都灵全国美术博览会上展出的大型作品《云》，与他本人的自信相反，遭到了充满敌意的批评。晚年的丰塔内西重新诠释了此前吸收的柯罗和透纳的教益，执着追寻“真实”的风景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/21-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《有云的风景》1880年左右 铅笔・墨水・水彩／纸 都灵市立现代和当代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/22-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《云》1880年 油彩／画布 都灵市立现代和当代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/23-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西《圣毛罗波河日落》1878‒1881年左右 油彩／画布 都灵市立现代和当代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第8章：丰塔内西的遗产（1872-1928年）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对风景的注视、人与自然的关系、空气与光的描绘——在丰塔内西去世后，他的艺术遗产被后代艺术家所继承。受过他指导的恩里科·莱切多、参与其身后回顾展的雕塑家莱奥纳尔多·比斯托尔菲、继承了丰富抒情性的米兰“羞耻派”（Scapigliatura）画画家们、在母题层面积极拓展其遗产的朱塞佩·佩里扎·达·沃尔佩多，以及通过推崇与评价表达敬意的卡尔洛·卡拉和费利切·卡索拉蒂。形式虽各不相同，但丰塔内西留下的精神依然在许多意大利艺术家的作品中呼吸着。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/24-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "朱塞佩·佩里扎·达·沃尔佩多《蒙齐尼牧场上的两个牧羊人（十一月）》1901年 油彩／画布 都灵市立现代和当代美术馆 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西（1818-1882）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/25.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西肖像照 1878年拍摄 松户市教育委员会藏", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1818年出生于意大利北部雷焦艾米利亚，并在当地美术学校学习。1848年作为志愿兵投身第一次意大利独立战争，退役后逃亡瑞士。以日内瓦为活动据点，同时造访巴黎并在法国南部进行创作。1859年随军参加第二次意大利独立战争，同年返回日内瓦。在向巴黎沙龙参展并逗留伦敦、佛罗伦萨之后，撤销了日内瓦的工作室，于1868年就任卢卡美术学院校长兼教授，次年1869年就任都灵阿尔贝蒂娜美术学院风景画教授。应日本工部美术学校招募画学教师之邀，于1876年来日，但因健康恶化等原因于2年后回国。1879年复职阿尔贝蒂娜美术学院，此后在指导后进的同时，以都灵为据点继续创作。1882年在都灵逝世，享年64岁。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "安东尼奥·丰塔内西过去往往仅被作为开拓近代日本西洋画史的教育家来谈论。然而其真实面貌却是一位罕见的画家，他在游历欧洲各地的同时追寻光与自然的神秘，并在意大利近代风景画中留下了坚实的足迹。本展作为其在日本的首次大型回顾展，汇聚了来自意大利各地收藏的名品、版画以及浅井忠等弟子们的作品，让人们能够尽情领略这位画家多方面的魅力与先进的绘画世界。不妨亲身体验一下由戏剧性的光影与丰富诗情交织而成的风景画精髓吧。（美术展Navi）", "translated": true}]

"全く知らない、という人もいるでしょう。美術に関心のある方ならば「明治時代に西洋絵画を教えたお雇い外国人」と答えるかもしれません。また洋画に詳しい方ならば浅井忠や小山正太郎の先生としての姿や、高橋由一との交友を思い浮かべるかもしれません。こうした反応が示すのは、第一にフォンタネージの名前が十分に知られていない、ということ。そして知っている人にとっても、お雇い外国人としてのイメージが強い、ということです。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "英雄ガリバルディの下でイタリア独立戦争に身を投じた兵士。ジュネーヴの都市風景を巧みに表した石版画家。パリのサロンに作品を発表し、当地でミレーやコローを研究するモダンな画家。ロンドンに滞在して版画を制作しつつ、ターナーやコンスタブルを吸収する旅人。フィレンツェの若手画家たちに信頼されるベテラン。南仏の田舎道を友人と歩く風景画家。トリノでも東京でも教え子から慕われる教育者。これらはすべて、「アントニオ・フォンタネージ」というひとりの人間の側面です。何度も同じ主題を取り上げつつ、理想の風景を絵画にしようとする姿勢、都市の忙しさや農村の労働に対する真摯な眼差し、そして何よりも、光と自然への探求。作品に目を凝らせば、「モティーフを高らかに歌わせよ！（La faccia cantar alto il suo motivo！）」と弟子たちに説いたフォンタネージの姿が見えてきます。フォンタネージを全く知らない人にとってはもちろん、名前を聞いたことがある人にとっても新しい。そんな風景画の旅が、いま、幕を開けます。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "日本イタリア国交樹立160周年記念／フォンタネージ来日150周年記念 フォンタネージ――イタリアの光・心の風景"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会場：三菱一号館美術館（東京都千代田区丸の内2-6-2）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会期：2026年10月17日（土）～2027年1月24日（日）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "paragraph", "text": "本展は、イタリア近代風景画の巨匠フォンタネージの日本初の大回顧展です。初期から晩年に至るまでの油彩画や、スイスや英国を旅して制作した版画などを含む約200点により、お雇い外国人に留まらないフォンタネージの魅力が明らかになります。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2-22.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《朝》1855‒1858年頃 油彩／厚紙に貼った紙 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "また、フォンタネージ来日から150年を経て、師と弟子たちの作品が集結する貴重な機会でもあります。本展では、イタリアから来日する作品群に加え、国内の美術・博物館所蔵のフォンタネージ作品、浅井忠、小山正太郎ら弟子たちの作品も一堂に会します。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/3-21.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "フォンタネージ送別記念写真 1878年撮影 松戸市教育委員会所蔵", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "そして、本展ではフォンタネージの先進性についても検証を加えます。展示室では、セガンティーニやカルロ・カッラなど、後世の画家たちの作品もあわせて披露され、彼が20世紀イタリアの芸術家たちどのような影響を与えてきたのか検証していきます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "展覧会構成"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第1章：「絵画」としての風景（1850-1860年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "故郷レッジョ・エミリアで美術の専門教育を受けたフォンタネージは、第一次イタリア独立戦争に参加した後、スイスのルガノ、次いでジュネーヴに拠点を移しました。美的な構図と「ピクチャレスク」な景色の追求から、風景画家・フォンタネージの歩みが始まります。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/4-22.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《岩の間の植物》1850年頃 油彩／厚紙 ビエッラ地域博物館（ビエッラ）Archivio Fotografico ‒ Museo del Territorio Biellese", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/5-21.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《ブジェイ高原》1859‒1860年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第2章：心をうつす風景（1855-1875年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1855年、バルビゾン派の画家トロワイヨンとともにパリ万博を訪問したフォンタネージは、コローや他のバルビゾン派の画家の作品に触れる機会を持ちました。これをきっかけのひとつとして、フォンタネージは自然に忠実であるだけでなく、繊細かつ抒情的な気分を取り入れた絵画の制作をはじめます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/6-19.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《水車小屋》 1858‒1859年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/7-20.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《静寂》1860年頃 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第3章：都市の風景（1854-1880年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "スイスへの移住、英国滞在、イタリア各地への旅の中で、フォンタネージは都市の風景に目を向けます。ジュネーヴ市内に取材したリトグラフに始まるフォンタネージの都市風景は、アルバム『ロンドンのスケッチ』でより洗練され、イタリアの外光派・マッキアイオーリの画家たちとの交友を育んだフィレンツェ滞在、アルベルティーナ美術アカデミーへの招聘を契機としたトリノへの移住を経て、彼の都市への関心はさらに強化されました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/8-18.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《サンタ・マリア・ノヴェッラ聖堂》1867年頃 油彩／板 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/9-18.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《フィレンツェの旧市場》1867年頃 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/10-16.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《ビッグ・ベン》1865‒1866年 油彩／厚紙 個人蔵 Collezione privata Degiovanni Dante, Italia Photo courtesy: Sant’Agostino Casa d’Aste, Torino.Photo: Guido Lovisolo", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/11-15.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《ロンドン、ラドゲート・ヒルより望むセント・ポール大聖堂》1866年 クリシェ・ヴェール トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第4章：日々の仕事と自然（1860-1875年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "パリのサロンへの出展を通して、ローザ・ボヌールやジャン＝フランソワ・ミレーらの絵画に触れたフォンタネージは、1860年ごろから次第に日常生活や社会に根差した主題の探求をはじめます。農民や家畜、そして人間と自然の関係に重きを置いたフォンタネージの作品は、彼の画業における重要な転換点を示しています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/12-15.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《労働》1868‒1872年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/13-9.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《物思いにふける羊飼い》1861‒1863年 油彩／板 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/14-8.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《厩舎》1860‒1865年 油彩／板 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第5章：一瞬の光を描いて（1867-1880年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "フォンタネージは光の変化を感情の起伏と結びつけました。雲が太陽を遮った瞬間、平原に虹色の光が放たれるその一瞬を切り取った《四月》、日没時の光の変化に従って風景が変容していく様を描いた沼地の連作――気象と光の移ろい、そしてその効果に着目し、不安定かつ神秘的な自然を、フォンタネージは丹念に絵画化します。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/15-7.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《四月》1873年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/16-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《沼に沈む太陽》1874年頃 油彩／板 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/17-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《沼の落日》1876‒1878年頃 油彩／画布 三重県立美術館", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第6章：日本での制作と教育（1876-1878年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "明治政府により設立された工部美術学校の画学教師に任命されたフォンタネージは1876年8月頃に東京に到着しました。およそ2年後の1878年秋、健康上の理由や学校の改革の頓挫等により帰国したフォンタネージでしたが、体系的な教育の試みや熱心な指導は、女子生徒を含む教え子との間の実りある対話と信頼関係をもたらしました。浅井忠、小山正太郎、松岡壽をはじめとする生徒たちは師の教えを様々に昇華し、その後の洋画の基礎を築きます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/18-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《日本の寺の入り口》1878‒1880年 キアロスクーロ／画布 レッジョ・エミリア市立博物館　Musei Civici Reggio Emilia", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/19-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "浅井忠 《徳川家の霊廟Ⅰ（寺の入り口Ⅰ）》1878年頃 油彩／紙 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "小山正太郎《秋景図》1887年 油彩／画布 京都国立近代美術館寄託", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第7章：晩年の作品（1878-1881年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帰国後、フォンタネージはアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーでの仕事を再開します。しかし、1880年のトリノ国民美術博覧会に出品された大作《雲》は、本人の自信とは裏腹に敵意のある批評にさらされてしまいます。晩年のフォンタネージは、今まで吸収したコローやターナーの教訓を再解釈し、「真実」の風景を追い求めます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/21-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《雲のある風景》1880年頃 鉛筆・インク・水彩／紙 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/22-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《雲》1880年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/23-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ《サン・マウロのポー川に沈む夕日》1878‒1881年頃 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "第8章：フォンタネージの遺産（1872-1928年）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "風景へのまなざし、人間と自然との関係、空気と光の描写――フォンタネージの死後、彼の芸術的遺産は次世代の芸術家に受け継がれます。彼の指導を受けたエンリコ・レイチェンドや没後の回顧展に関与した彫刻家レオナルド・ビストルフィ、豊かな抒情性を継承したミラノのスカピリアトゥーラ運動の画家たち、モティーフの面でその遺産を展開させたジュゼッペ・ペリッツァ・ダ・ヴォルペード、顕彰と評価によって敬意を表したカルロ・カッラやフェリーチェ・カゾラーティ。かたちは様々ですが、多くのイタリアの芸術家の作品に、フォンタネージの遺したものは息づいています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/24-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ジュゼッペ・ペリッツァ・ダ・ヴォルペード《モンジーニの牧草地にいる二人の羊飼い（十一月）》1901年 油彩／画布 トリノ市立近現代美術館 GAM – Galleria Civica d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea, Torino. Courtesy Fondazione Torino Musei", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ（1818-1882）"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/25.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "アントニオ・フォンタネージ肖像写真　1878年撮影　松戸市教育委員会所蔵", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1818年、イタリア北部レッジョ・エミリアに生まれ、当地の美術学校に学ぶ。1848年、第1次イタリア独立戦争に志願兵として身を投じ、除隊後スイスに逃避。ジュネーヴを拠点に活動すると同時にパリ訪問や南仏での制作も行う。1859年、第2次イタリア独立戦争に従軍、同年ジュネーヴに戻る。パリのサロンへの出品やロンドン、フィレンツェへの滞在ののちジュネーヴのアトリエを引き払い、1868年にルッカの美術アカデミーの校長兼教授、翌1869年にトリノのアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーの風景画教授に就任する。日本の工部美術学校の画学教師の募集に応じ、1876年に来日するものの体調の悪化などを理由に2年で帰国。1879年にアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーに復職し、以降後進を指導する傍ら、トリノを拠点に制作を続けた。1882年、トリノにて没。享年64。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "近代日本の洋画史を切り拓いた教育者としてのみ語られがちだったアントニオ・フォンタネージ。しかしその実像は、ヨーロッパ各地を巡りながら光と自然の神秘を追い求め、イタリア近代風景画に確固たる足跡を残した類まれなる画家でした。日本初の大回顧展となる本展では、イタリア各地のコレクションから集結する名品や版画、そして浅井忠ら弟子たちの作品が一堂に会し、画家の多面的な魅力と先進的な絵画世界を存分に堪能することができます。劇的な光と豊かな詩情が織りなす風景画の真髄をぜひ味わってみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）"}]

19世紀イタリアを代表する風景画の巨匠

三菱一号館美術館(東京・丸の内)で10月17日に始まった「フォンタネージ―イタリアの光・心の風景」。前日に行われた内覧会で取材しました。 詩情あふれる風景画の名作の数々を、同館ならではの落ち着いた空間でじっくり味わえます。

アントニオ・フォンタネージ(1818-1882)は明治時代のはじめに日本へ招聘。浅井忠や小山正太郎らを育て、西洋美術の礎を築いた「お雇い外国人」として名高いです。

今展では19世紀イタリアを代表する風景画家として活躍した彼の画業を幅広く紹介。その全容を明らかにします。

若き日本の画家からも慕われた存在

高い技量と熱心な指導で美術を目指す若き日本人たちから慕われたフォンタネージ。イタリアの続く世代にも影響を与えました。東西の後進たちの作品もあわせて紹介され、フォンタネージの存在の大きさを実感できます。

「フォンタネージ―イタリアの光・心の風景」三菱一号館美術館(東京・丸の内)で2027年1月24日(日)まで。

イタリア近代風景画の巨匠、日本初の大回顧展が京都から東京へ。約200点で充実の画業を振り返ります。来年2月には名古屋市美術館に巡回します。（美術展ナビ編集班 岡部匡志） 以下はプレビュー記事です。詳しくは↓

三菱一号館美術館（東京都千代田区）で、「フォンタネージ――イタリアの光・心の風景」が10月17日から開催されます。

あなたはアントニオ・フォンタネージという画家を知っていますか？

全く知らない、という人もいるでしょう。美術に関心のある方ならば「明治時代に西洋絵画を教えたお雇い外国人」と答えるかもしれません。また洋画に詳しい方ならば浅井忠や小山正太郎の先生としての姿や、高橋由一との交友を思い浮かべるかもしれません。こうした反応が示すのは、第一にフォンタネージの名前が十分に知られていない、ということ。そして知っている人にとっても、お雇い外国人としてのイメージが強い、ということです。

英雄ガリバルディの下でイタリア独立戦争に身を投じた兵士。ジュネーヴの都市風景を巧みに表した石版画家。パリのサロンに作品を発表し、当地でミレーやコローを研究するモダンな画家。ロンドンに滞在して版画を制作しつつ、ターナーやコンスタブルを吸収する旅人。フィレンツェの若手画家たちに信頼されるベテラン。南仏の田舎道を友人と歩く風景画家。トリノでも東京でも教え子から慕われる教育者。これらはすべて、「アントニオ・フォンタネージ」というひとりの人間の側面です。何度も同じ主題を取り上げつつ、理想の風景を絵画にしようとする姿勢、都市の忙しさや農村の労働に対する真摯な眼差し、そして何よりも、光と自然への探求。作品に目を凝らせば、「モティーフを高らかに歌わせよ！（La faccia cantar alto il suo motivo！）」と弟子たちに説いたフォンタネージの姿が見えてきます。フォンタネージを全く知らない人にとってはもちろん、名前を聞いたことがある人にとっても新しい。そんな風景画の旅が、いま、幕を開けます。

日本イタリア国交樹立160周年記念／フォンタネージ来日150周年記念 フォンタネージ――イタリアの光・心の風景

会場：三菱一号館美術館（東京都千代田区丸の内2-6-2）

会期：2026年10月17日（土）～2027年1月24日（日）

開館時間：10:00～18:00（金曜日、第2水曜日、会期最終週の平日は20:00まで） ※入館は閉館の30分前まで

休館日：月曜日（ただし、祝日、トークフリーデー［10/26、11/30、12/28］、および1/18は開館）、12/31、1/1

観覧料：一般2,300円、大学生1,300円、高校生1,000円、中学生以下無料 ※障害者手帳をお持ちの方は半額、付添の方1名まで無料

アクセス： JR「東京」駅（丸の内南口）徒歩5分 JR「有楽町」駅（国際フォーラム口）徒歩6分 東京メトロ千代田線「二重橋前〈丸の内〉」駅（1番出口）徒歩3分

詳細は、 三菱一号館美術館公式サイト（展覧会サイト） まで。

本展の見どころ

本展は、イタリア近代風景画の巨匠フォンタネージの日本初の大回顧展です。初期から晩年に至るまでの油彩画や、スイスや英国を旅して制作した版画などを含む約200点により、お雇い外国人に留まらないフォンタネージの魅力が明らかになります。

また、フォンタネージ来日から150年を経て、師と弟子たちの作品が集結する貴重な機会でもあります。本展では、イタリアから来日する作品群に加え、国内の美術・博物館所蔵のフォンタネージ作品、浅井忠、小山正太郎ら弟子たちの作品も一堂に会します。

そして、本展ではフォンタネージの先進性についても検証を加えます。展示室では、セガンティーニやカルロ・カッラなど、後世の画家たちの作品もあわせて披露され、彼が20世紀イタリアの芸術家たちどのような影響を与えてきたのか検証していきます。

展覧会構成

第1章：「絵画」としての風景（1850-1860年）

故郷レッジョ・エミリアで美術の専門教育を受けたフォンタネージは、第一次イタリア独立戦争に参加した後、スイスのルガノ、次いでジュネーヴに拠点を移しました。美的な構図と「ピクチャレスク」な景色の追求から、風景画家・フォンタネージの歩みが始まります。

第2章：心をうつす風景（1855-1875年）

1855年、バルビゾン派の画家トロワイヨンとともにパリ万博を訪問したフォンタネージは、コローや他のバルビゾン派の画家の作品に触れる機会を持ちました。これをきっかけのひとつとして、フォンタネージは自然に忠実であるだけでなく、繊細かつ抒情的な気分を取り入れた絵画の制作をはじめます。

第3章：都市の風景（1854-1880年）

スイスへの移住、英国滞在、イタリア各地への旅の中で、フォンタネージは都市の風景に目を向けます。ジュネーヴ市内に取材したリトグラフに始まるフォンタネージの都市風景は、アルバム『ロンドンのスケッチ』でより洗練され、イタリアの外光派・マッキアイオーリの画家たちとの交友を育んだフィレンツェ滞在、アルベルティーナ美術アカデミーへの招聘を契機としたトリノへの移住を経て、彼の都市への関心はさらに強化されました。

第4章：日々の仕事と自然（1860-1875年）

パリのサロンへの出展を通して、ローザ・ボヌールやジャン＝フランソワ・ミレーらの絵画に触れたフォンタネージは、1860年ごろから次第に日常生活や社会に根差した主題の探求をはじめます。農民や家畜、そして人間と自然の関係に重きを置いたフォンタネージの作品は、彼の画業における重要な転換点を示しています。

第5章：一瞬の光を描いて（1867-1880年）

フォンタネージは光の変化を感情の起伏と結びつけました。雲が太陽を遮った瞬間、平原に虹色の光が放たれるその一瞬を切り取った《四月》、日没時の光の変化に従って風景が変容していく様を描いた沼地の連作――気象と光の移ろい、そしてその効果に着目し、不安定かつ神秘的な自然を、フォンタネージは丹念に絵画化します。

第6章：日本での制作と教育（1876-1878年）

明治政府により設立された工部美術学校の画学教師に任命されたフォンタネージは1876年8月頃に東京に到着しました。およそ2年後の1878年秋、健康上の理由や学校の改革の頓挫等により帰国したフォンタネージでしたが、体系的な教育の試みや熱心な指導は、女子生徒を含む教え子との間の実りある対話と信頼関係をもたらしました。浅井忠、小山正太郎、松岡壽をはじめとする生徒たちは師の教えを様々に昇華し、その後の洋画の基礎を築きます。

第7章：晩年の作品（1878-1881年）

帰国後、フォンタネージはアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーでの仕事を再開します。しかし、1880年のトリノ国民美術博覧会に出品された大作《雲》は、本人の自信とは裏腹に敵意のある批評にさらされてしまいます。晩年のフォンタネージは、今まで吸収したコローやターナーの教訓を再解釈し、「真実」の風景を追い求めます。

第8章：フォンタネージの遺産（1872-1928年）

風景へのまなざし、人間と自然との関係、空気と光の描写――フォンタネージの死後、彼の芸術的遺産は次世代の芸術家に受け継がれます。彼の指導を受けたエンリコ・レイチェンドや没後の回顧展に関与した彫刻家レオナルド・ビストルフィ、豊かな抒情性を継承したミラノのスカピリアトゥーラ運動の画家たち、モティーフの面でその遺産を展開させたジュゼッペ・ペリッツァ・ダ・ヴォルペード、顕彰と評価によって敬意を表したカルロ・カッラやフェリーチェ・カゾラーティ。かたちは様々ですが、多くのイタリアの芸術家の作品に、フォンタネージの遺したものは息づいています。

アントニオ・フォンタネージ（1818-1882）

1818年、イタリア北部レッジョ・エミリアに生まれ、当地の美術学校に学ぶ。1848年、第1次イタリア独立戦争に志願兵として身を投じ、除隊後スイスに逃避。ジュネーヴを拠点に活動すると同時にパリ訪問や南仏での制作も行う。1859年、第2次イタリア独立戦争に従軍、同年ジュネーヴに戻る。パリのサロンへの出品やロンドン、フィレンツェへの滞在ののちジュネーヴのアトリエを引き払い、1868年にルッカの美術アカデミーの校長兼教授、翌1869年にトリノのアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーの風景画教授に就任する。日本の工部美術学校の画学教師の募集に応じ、1876年に来日するものの体調の悪化などを理由に2年で帰国。1879年にアルベルティーナ美術アカデミーに復職し、以降後進を指導する傍ら、トリノを拠点に制作を続けた。1882年、トリノにて没。享年64。

近代日本の洋画史を切り拓いた教育者としてのみ語られがちだったアントニオ・フォンタネージ。しかしその実像は、ヨーロッパ各地を巡りながら光と自然の神秘を追い求め、イタリア近代風景画に確固たる足跡を残した類まれなる画家でした。日本初の大回顧展となる本展では、イタリア各地のコレクションから集結する名品や版画、そして浅井忠ら弟子たちの作品が一堂に会し、画家の多面的な魅力と先進的な絵画世界を存分に堪能することができます。劇的な光と豊かな詩情が織りなす風景画の真髄をぜひ味わってみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
Ghulam Ali Khan, Two Men Wrestling, Tashrih-al-Aqvam, Gouache on Paper. 1825 AD.

The first thing one notices about an akhara is the earth. Carefully maintained—turned over, watered and sometimes scented—it forms the centre of the wrestling pit. Early in the morning, before the heat settles in, wrestlers step onto it barefoot. Some touch the ground before entering; others rub earth onto their arms and chest. The smell is distinctive: mustard oil, ghee, sweat and soil. Earth and bodies mingle in a way that feels almost consecrated. This is where wrestlers train, compete, exchange stories and spend long hours together. Outsiders rarely find their way inside. Akharas are not public spaces in the conventional sense but tightly knit communities held together by routines, hierarchies and a shared devotion to wrestling.

When we encounter wrestlers in Indian miniature painting, a different set of questions emerges. Who is looking at these bodies? What drew the artist’s eye? What did audiences see? Strength? Skill? Masculinity? Or something else entirely?

Looking at a nineteenth-century miniature depicting two wrestlers in practice, I am struck by something unexpected. The scene is deceptively simple. Two men are locked in a grappling hold while jori clubs and weights lie scattered about. These men clearly embody strength and physical discipline, yet there is remarkably little emphasis on muscle itself. What stands out is not the muscularity of the wrestlers but its relative absence.

Seen alongside other depictions of wrestling from the Mughal and colonial periods, the image points toward a broader visual tradition in which bodily strength was understood differently from how it often is today. Whether wrestlers appear grappling before Emperor Shah Jahan, entertaining courtly audiences, or training amidst clubs, weights and fellow practitioners, the emphasis rarely falls on the detailed rendering of muscular anatomy. The men are undoubtedly powerful, yet painters seem more interested in wrestling itself and the social worlds surrounding it. Wrestling appears simultaneously as discipline, spectacle, performance and patronage.

Mir Kalan Khan, Painting of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan Watching a Wrestling Match, Delhi or Lucknow. Gouache on Paper. 1750 AD.

Today fitness culture encourages us to associate strength with visible muscularity. Whether scrolling through Instagram, watching fitness influencers on YouTube or passing advertisements for gyms, we encounter bodies designed to be admired. Defined abdominals, broad shoulders and pronounced biceps have become visual shorthand for health and physical power. The wrestlers in these miniatures suggest a different ideal. Their bodies appear compact and functional rather than sculpted for display. What matters is not appearance but action. The emphasis falls on movement, leverage, balance and technique. Strength resides in what the body can do rather than how it looks.

Historically, Indian wrestling cultivated a distinctive understanding of bodily development. Wrestlers trained intensely and followed demanding routines of exercise, diet and discipline. They sought endurance, resilience and stamina alongside strength. The goal was not simply to build a body but to cultivate a particular way of life. The training equipment depicted in miniature painting points toward this broader world. Indian clubs, or mugdars, have long been associated with wrestling traditions. During the nineteenth century they travelled far beyond South Asia, becoming popular exercise tools in Europe and North America before largely disappearing and then recently returning through contemporary fitness culture. What appears innovative is often a reworking of much older practices.

Yet the relationship between wrestling and bodybuilding is far from straightforward. Wrestling has undoubtedly shaped broader ideas about masculinity, discipline and physical strength in India. Throughout the twentieth century wrestlers became symbols of masculine achievement and national pride, while physical culture movements drew inspiration from wrestling traditions alongside influences from Europe and North America. At the same time, wrestling and bodybuilding do not produce identical bodies.

The wrestler’s physique emerges through grappling, swinging clubs, performing dands and baithaks, and training with opponents. Fitness and bodybuilding place far greater emphasis on the visual presentation of the body. It would be a mistake, however, to imagine that kushti wrestling has remained unchanged. Nowhere is this transformation more visible than on social media. Many younger wrestlers maintain active Instagram and YouTube accounts where they document training sessions, share dietary advice and post carefully composed photographs of their physiques. The body has become something to be viewed as much as something to be used. Visibility now matters in ways that would have been unfamiliar to the wrestlers depicted in older paintings. As a result, the physiques displayed by many contemporary wrestlers increasingly resemble those associated with bodybuilding.

Looking back at these paintings reveals not only how wrestling has changed but also how our ways of seeing bodies have changed. In one image wrestlers perform before a royal audience; in another British soldiers and Indian spectators observe demonstrations of physical training and martial exercise. Together these scenes remind us that wrestling was never simply about individual bodies. It connected rulers and subjects, teachers and pupils, spectators and performers. Strength derived meaning from these relationships rather than from the isolated display of muscle.

The wrestlers in traditional miniature paintings are presented differently from the bodies that dominate contemporary fitness culture. Their physiques matter, but they are rarely the central subject. Attention is directed instead toward movement, technique, ritual and the communities gathered around these practices. What emerges is a vision of strength that is fundamentally relational rather than individual. The muscular body was certainly present, but it had not yet become the primary object of attention that it would later become in the worlds of bodybuilding, fitness culture and social media.

title_original: Ibrahim Mahama’s Most Ambitious Show Yet Is Headed to Paris—But Its Core Is in Ghana
editorial_title_zh: 易卜拉欣·马哈马迄今最具雄心的展览将登陆巴黎——但其核心在加纳

article_text:
Listen to Ibrahim Mahama speak, and he’s likely to credit his success to his community, which includes market women, weavers, craftsmen, studio assistants, railway workers, curators, professors, and fellow artists.

The Ghanaian artist is quick to recognize their contributions when he receives one of the many awards he’s picked up recently. Ranked at the top of the influential ArtReview Power 100 list in 2025, he also won an Art Basel Gold Award that year and received the 2026 Arnold Bode prize. He was also recently named a chevalier of the French government’s Ordre des Arts et des Lettres; the honor was bestowed upon him in Ghana by Diarra Dime Labille, France’s Ambassador to the West African country.

“We live and work in a community and nobody is an island by themselves. I built my practice based on the idea of collectivity and working with different collaborators,” Mahama explained in an interview with ARTnews . As an example, he cited the scornful and at times suspicious reactions of Mallam Atta market women in Accra when he started collecting worn-out jute sacks at the early stage of his career, especially because he was still in college when he began producing those works. (The works he produced using those sacks quickly gained him fame, with some memorably appearing in Okwui Enwezor’s Venice Biennale in 2015.) As he spent time with the market women, they came to understand what he was doing and continued supporting him, helping him collect the sacks that still recur in his art.

“I think the artist is just a vessel, and I see myself as that vessel in order to put all these different things together to do the work that we do,” he added.

Mahama has become one of the most internationally visible Ghanaian artists, showing his work at biennials and museums across the world, and directing his success back to Ghana: The money from the sales of Mahama’s work is directed toward building institutions that he founds, including the Tamale-based Red Clay Studio and the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art. He’s also bought dilapidated or abandoned buildings, factories, and airplanes, and turned them into art and educational spaces, as he did with Nkrumah Voli-ni, also in Tamale.

These projects, which Mahama called a “lifetime work,” breathe new life into collected materials, archives, industrial and national heritage. His work at times extends beyond Ghana to include international like with people like the Kenyan British artist Michael Armitage and his Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute. Learning from those conversations and becoming part of a large community expands the scope of what is possible is Mahama’s practice.

On Thursday, Mahama will open yet another epic project: “The Harvest Season,” an exhibition at the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain in Paris, whose entire building he will take over starting next week. The show is “the most ambitious exhibition I’ve done,” Mahama said.

Parliament of Ghosts , an ongoing installation made of discarded train seats, railway sleepers, school furniture, worn-out jute sacks, and government archives that premiered in 2019 will figure in the Fondation Cartier show in a new iteration that adds about 200 collected and restored royal stools from the Asante Empire.

The idea, Mahama said, is to highlight a contradiction: These same stools, which are often looted before being exhibited in Western museums, are at times placed in glass cases. At the Fondation Cartier, people will have free access to them. He hopes this will invert questions around the return of African objects from Europe, asking: What happens when these stools are brought from Ghana to Europe as “living” objects and utilized for their original purpose, and not in museum cases or glasses? Doing so brings out the “the ghosts [and] histories” of these stools, creating an avenue for different conversations, he added.

There’s also a new project created by Mahama for this exhibition centered on the Aboso Glass Factory, which was established in 1966 by Ghana’s first president, Kwame Nkrumah, as part of the country’s industrialization efforts, before he was overthrown in a coup in that same year. Titled Things Fall Apart, after the 1958 novel by Nigerian author Chinua Achebe, it is a reconstruction of the abandoned glass bottle manufacturing plant that Mahama purchased some two years ago with production funds from Fondation Cartier.

The Paris installation is only a small part of the project, however, since the glass factory is being rebuilt in spaces including Red Clay Studio in Tamale and a British-era colonial building. When the Fondation Cartier exhibition ends, the factory will be returned to Ghana for permanent installation in Kumasi, where Mahama plans to build a new institution. He is also working with cinema owners and local craftsmen to explore the possibility of rebuilding some abandoned cinemas in the country.

In addition, a collection of works on the Ghanaian railway system will also be on display in the exhibition. A new textile installation using Ghanaian fabrics produced in northern Ghana, truck inner tubes, jute sacks, and found textiles will be hung across the arcades on the facades of the Fondation Cartier building.

“There is a dialogue between this old building [constructed in the 1850s] and Ibrahim’s work, which addresses the history of the 19th century in Ghana, and the links between what was happening between Europe and West Africa at that time,” said Aby Gaye-Duparc, the curator of the exhibition.

“What we really want to convey to the audience is that there are two sides of [Mahama]’s artistic practice,” said Gaye-Duparc. “There’s work that we see: installations, videos, work on paper. Everything comes from this community in Tamale that he has built because a lot of the installations were made first in Tamale and then travel to Paris or other venues.”

The other part, Gaye-Duparc continued, “is the work behind it that is being built in Tamale,” referring to the artist’s building of artistic infrastructure and institutions in the Northern Ghana city. These structures, she added, have expanded access to the arts for people who were left out for various reasons.

In line with Mahama’s collaborative approach, the Paris exhibition will also feature work by artists and collectives including James Barnor, Gideon Appah, CATPC (Cercle d’Art des Travailleurs de Plantation Congolaise), Tjaša Rener, Postbox Ghana, Courage Dzidula Kpodo, and Dorothy Akpene Amenuke, Mahama’s mentor.

Kpodo, an architect, will exhibit work that addresses modernism, turning the focus away from tropical modernism centered on concrete buildings, which were often built by foreigners in Ghanaian cities. The central piece will be a wall reconstruction made out of laterite from a building he owns in Gyampo, in the Eastern Region, used in so-called vernacular or traditional buildings. The installation will include about 100 postcards by the Postbox Ghana collective depicting tropical modernist architectural buildings in cities such as Accra, Kumasi and Takoradi.

“I would describe Ibrahim as someone who makes space within his own abilities and means for people that he thinks are doing interesting, important work,” said Kpodo.

The Fondation Cartier exhibition is one of the first major ones by Mahama staged since he was viciously attacked earlier this year by a special operations unit of the Ghana Police Service in Tamale, where he lives and works. Mahama noted the community support that he received during the fallout, saying, “It was fantastic, I must say. I was really overwhelmed, because sometimes you don’t realize how much your work means to people.” He added that people traveled from within Tamale and from other cities like Accra and Kumasi came to visit him, express regret, and bemoan the treatment meted out to him by the police, especially because of his considerable contributions to the city.

He said he was unaware of the current state of the investigations into the matter by the Criminal Investigation Department as directed by Ghana’s Inspector General of Police because he hadn’t received updates in months. But he also seemed more interested in concentrating on his art. “I want to channel my energy into this positive part of my practice of what I do and what it means to the community,” he explained. “But certainly, I am also quite disappointed in the way that it was handled by the police. And I hope that at some point, we will be able to at least know more [about the investigations], so that we see what direction to take it in.” He plans to follow up again when he settles back in Ghana by the end of the year from his travels.

For now, he is more focused on supporting the community he has helped create. “I’m happy that the work I do has a very profound meaning and effect on people who live on our continent, in particular Ghana. I am also interested in how this work is traveling around the world, stretching the African sensibilities, and what we are bringing to art in the 21st century.”
excerpt_original: The Fondation Cartier exhibition is related to Mahama’s larger project of bridging Ghana’s art community and the rest of the world.

Cartelera de Cinépolis – Estrenos del 5 de noviembre, 2026

Staff Cine PREMIERE

¿Qué verás esta semana?

Esta semana la cartelera Cinépolis se renueva con una selección de estrenos que van desde grandes producciones comerciales hasta propuestas más arriesgadas para quienes buscan algo distinto en la sala de cine. Ya sea que tengas ganas de una historia emotiva, un thriller intenso o puro entretenimiento para desconectarte, los nuevos lanzamientos ofrecen opciones para todos los gustos. ¿Qué películas nuevas llegan a la cartelera de Cinépolis? Entérate aquí.

Aquí te contamos cuáles son las películas que llegan a la cartelera Cinépolis esta semana y la siguiente. Una guía rápida para decidir qué ver, cuándo ir y no perderte los títulos más comentados del momento.

Cartelera Cinépolis: estrenos del jueves 5 de noviembre de 2026

Ceniza en la boca / Dir. Diego Luna / México, España / 2026

Ceniza en la boca / Dir. Diego Luna / México, España / 2026 Lucila, de 21 años, se muda a España con su hermano para reunirse con su madre, quien los abandonó hace ocho años. Enfrentándose a la discriminación y las responsabilidades familiares, lucha por encontrar su independencia mientras lidia con las heridas del pasado.

Gozilla menos cero (Godzilla Minus Zero) / Dir. Takashi Yamazaki / Japón / 2026 La familia Shikishima se enfrenta a una amenaza completamente nueva con el regreso de Godzilla, que sembrará el caos.

Klara y el sol (Klara and the Sun) / Dir. Taika Waititi / Reino Unido, India, EE. UU. / 2026 Una niña robot diseñada para prevenir la soledad intenta salvar a una familia de humanos desconsolada.

El gato con sombrero (The Cat in the Hat) / Dirs. Alessandro Carloni, Erica Rivinoja / EE. UU. / 2026 El gato con sombrero se enfrenta a su misión más difícil hasta ahora para el I.I.I.I. (Instituto para la Institución de la Imaginación e Inspiración, S.A.): animar a Gabby y Sebastián, dos hermanos que están teniendo dificultades para adaptarse a su nueva ciudad. Conocido por siempre llevar las cosas al extremo, esta podría ser la última oportunidad de este agente del caos para demostrar su valía… o perder su sombrero mágico.

Grin, el juego de la oiuja (Grin) / Dir. Lawrence Fowler / Reino Unido / 2026 Eva visita a su familia y conoce a Lucian, la nueva pareja de su madre, quien le presenta un inquietante juego de mesa antiguo. Lo que comienza como un juego divertido se torna mortal cuando desata una entidad demoníaca que persigue a los jugadores con oscuros secretos, haciéndolos desaparecer uno a uno.

Caballo salvaje nueve (Wild Horse Nine) / Dir. Martin McDonagh / Reino Unido, EE. UU., Chile / 2026 Los agentes de la CIA Chris y Lee se enfrentan a una misión de prueba de confianza desde Santiago hasta la Isla de Pascua durante 1973 en Chile.

La venus eléctrica (La Vénus électrique) / Dir. Pierre Salvadori / Francia, Bélgica / 2026 En el París de 1928, un pintor, incapaz de trabajar desde la muerte de su esposa, participa sin saberlo en falsos espectáculos espiritistas organizados por un feriante. A medida que recupera la inspiración, ella se enamora del hombre al que está engañando.

Rocky – 50 aniversario (Rocky) – reestreno / Dir. John G. Avildsen / EE. UU. / 2026 Un boxeador de poca monta de Filadelfia tiene una oportunidad sumamente excepcional de enfrentarse al campeón mundial de peso pesado en un combate en el que luchará por llegar hasta el final para preservar su dignidad.

También te podría interesar: Cartelera de Cinépolis – Estrenos de esta semana .

¿Qué llegará la próxima semana a la cartelera Cinépolis (jueves 12 de noviembre 2026)?

No, gracias, ya no fumo / Dir. Diego Toussaint / México / 2026

Yo soy Rocky (I Play Rocky) / Dir. Peter Farrelly / EE. UU. / 2026 La historia real de un actor desconocido que creía que su destino no era solo escribir Rocky , sino interpretar a Rocky Balboa. Ante el rechazo constante, Sylvester Stallone lo arriesga todo, negándose a renunciar al papel principal contra todo pronóstico.

Cómo robar un banco (How to Rob a Bank) / Dir. David Leitch / EE. UU. / 2026 Unos atracadores de bancos publican sus robos en las redes sociales, lo que provoca que la policía los persiga.

Ramayana: el nacimiento de una leyenda (Ramayana: Rise of a Legend) / India, EE. UU., Reino Unido / 2026 Una antigua epopeya narra la historia de un joven príncipe y una princesa cuyo matrimonio y posterior exilio marcan el inicio de un viaje legendario. Su historia de amor, deber y destino sienta las bases para mayores desafíos que les esperan.

Petardos y magnolias / Dir.a Sandra Concepción Reynoso Estrada / México / 2026 Vera, una estudiante de secundaria apasionada por el futbol, se enamora de Alan, un joven prodigio de la tecnología vinculado a una peligrosa banda. Su incipiente romance desafía los planes de su padre para su carrera de abogada. Los lazos criminales de Alan amenazan su futuro, culminando en una gran decepción amorosa.

Saga Los juegos del hambre – Reestreno de las cinco películas Antes del estreno de Los juegos del hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha , las cinco películas de la saga vuelven a las salas para que revivas la historia de Katniss Everdeen desde la primera cosecha hasta la revolución de Sinsajo , y también los orígenes de Coriolanus Snow en Balada de pájaros cantores y serpientes . Una oportunidad perfecta para ponerte al día con el universo creado por Suzanne Collins… y que la suerte esté siempre de tu lado.

No, gracias, ya no fumo / Dir. Diego Toussaint / México / 2026 Tras ser despedida de su trabajo, Nuria tiene 24 horas para pagar el alquiler o volver a vivir con su madre. Su día incluye encuentros incómodos con su ex, un pinchazo y unos pantalones rotos, además de lidiar con parientes entrometidos y artistas egocéntricos, todo ello mientras intenta no fumar.

article_text:
Sergei Loznitsa’s “Imperium,” which revisits the Soviet Union of the early 1970s through footage shot by Italian cameramen, has won the best film award at the 70th BFI London Film Festival competition.

The prizes were unveiled Sunday as the festival drew to a close. The competition jury was led by filmmaker Sam Pollard, whose credits include “MLK/FBI” and “Citizen Ashe,” and also featured “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” filmmaker Mariano Llinás and DDA chief strategy officer Julie La Bassiere.

Related Stories

Egyptian Cinema Eyes Its Next Act as Industry Veterans Call for Better Scripts, Wider Distribution

“The film is richly evocative and emotionally engaging on all levels giving us a visually arresting perspective of life before the Soviet Union was broken apart,” the jury said.

Popular on Variety

In the first feature competition, the Sutherland Award went to Thailand’s Oscar submission “9 Temples to Heaven,” the first fiction feature from Sompot Chidgasornpongse. The film reflects on faith, kinship and the passage from life to death. Actor Amir El-Masry (“Giant,” “Limbo”) presided over that jury, joined by “Moonglow” producer Alemberg Ang and sales, distribution and awards strategist Rosa Bosch.

“An accomplished first feature paving his own path in the well-established tradition of filmmaking in the Southeast Asian region,” the jury said.

Bertil Nilsson’s “Masc” received a special mention in the same section. The debut tracks Robin, who drifts between short-term jobs and uncertain relationships while looking for somewhere he fits. The jury singled out Nilsson as a fresh British talent with an unusual concept and a funny script.

The Grierson Award for documentary went to Asmahan Bkerat’s feature directorial debut “Concrete Land,” which spends time with several generations of a mixed-race family in Jordan as they resist displacement and hostility. “Santosh” director Sandhya Suri headed the documentary jury, alongside Melbourne International Film Festival senior programmer Kate Fitzpatrick and BAFTA and Emmy-winning producer Andee Ryder.

“In a noisy and often polemical world it was refreshing, humbling and deeply relevant to see the quiet resilience and dignity of this family in the face of the erasure of their culture and traditions,” the jury said.

Theo Rollason’s “Queer Edward II,” assembled entirely from archive material, earned a special mention. It goes behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s “Edward II,” set against the anti-LGBTQIA+ laws Britain passed in the 1980s, and the jury praised it as a portrait of Jarman the artist and Jarman the activist.

Rahul Roye’s “Aman” won the Short Film Award. The film centers on a trans man who learns he is pregnant the night before his gender-affirming surgery, upending his sense of who he is as a man and as a father. It is streaming free on BFI Player until Oct. 25.

Writer-producer Helen Simmons (“100 Nights of Hero”) led the shorts jury, which also included comedian Leo Reich and script editor Jack Casey.

“We were struck by the film’s painterly cinematography, and expansive and assured storytelling, which guided us through the world with care,” the jury said.

Elizabeth Hobbs’ “Daughters of the Late Colonel,” about two middle-aged sisters left adrift after the death of their domineering father, took a special mention for its inventive visual style.

Audience voting for the festival’s best feature film and best British discovery prizes closes Oct. 21, with winners to be named later. Last year, Chloé Zhao’s “Hamnet” took the audience prize for best feature, while Yemi Bamiro’s “Black Is Beautiful: The Kwame Brathwaite Story” won British discovery.

article_text:
Oscar-winning French actor Marion Cotillard will preside over the competition jury at the 23rd Marrakech Film Festival in November.

Alongside her to be announced jury members, the “Inception” and “Dark Knight Rises” star will lead the decision of which film is awarded the Étoile d’Or out of Marrakech’s international competition, which consists of first and second features.

“I have been fortunate enough to attend the Marrakech International Film Festival since its very beginnings; I’ve had wonderful experiences there and met some truly remarkable people,” Cotillard said in a statement. “Supporting filmmakers as they take their first steps is a vital part of what this festival is all about — it’s in its DNA — and it is a great joy for me to chair the jury this year.”

Related Stories

'La Bola Negra' to Receive Gotham Vanguard Tribute at Gotham Film Awards (EXCLUSIVE)

Queer Bodybuilder Drama 'Test' Acquired by Dark Star Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)

Cotillard first broke out in the 1998 French action comedy “Taxi,” before making her Hollywood debut in Tim Burton’s “Big Fish” in 2003. In 2007, she portrayed French singer Édith Piaf in “La Vie en Rose” and won the Oscar for best actress, becoming the first actor to win an Academy Award for a French-language performance. She earned her second best actress Oscar nomination in 2015 for the Dardenne Brothers’ drama “Two Days, One Night.”

Most recently, she starred in Guillaume Canet’s Cannes-premiering “Karma,” “Lee” alongside Kate Winslet and on the TV series “The Morning Show” opposite Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon. She is currently filming “The Enraged,” a historical drama from Emmanuelle Bercot.

This year’s Marrakech Film Festival takes place from Nov. 20-28.
